shadows.name: model-lift
shadows.purpose: The model card under the pointer, together with a 2px rise (Avalonia: 0 6 18 0 #38000000).

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Every entrance and state change: things rise into place and settle (Avalonia CubicEaseOut). No bounce or elastic curves.

motion.name: ease-exit
motion.purpose: A deleted card leaving the gallery (Avalonia CubicEaseIn).

motion.name: duration-feedback
motion.purpose: Selection ring 120ms, chip pop 140ms, card hover lift 150ms, details fade 160ms, drop overlay message 180ms.

motion.name: duration-exit
motion.purpose: Deleted card fades and shrinks to 95%; exits are faster than entrances.

motion.name: print-reveal
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: a freshly made thumbnail is uncovered bottom-up behind a 2px amber nozzle line (PrintReveal). Plays once per object.

motion.name: saved-hold
motion.purpose: How long 'Salvar Alterações' shows '✓ Salvo' after a save.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Set from the OS preference; drops the reveal and every lift, scale and rise while keeping fades and state colors.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Filament Spool"**

STLHub is styled after the printer. Its single accent is amber, like PLA glowing under an enclosure light. Its neutrals are warm browns and off-whites, like a spool core, a wooden bench and raw filament. Its structure works like a print's layers: orderly bands of toolbar, sidebar, gallery and details, stacked without fuss. It is a dense workshop catalogue for people who own hundreds or thousands of models. It is not a showroom and not a dashboard.

The chrome stays warm and quiet so the user's models are the most colorful thing on screen. Amber marks only what the user can act on next or what is currently selected: the open-library button, the save action, the selection ring and the busy indicator. Everything else is built from tonal steps of one warm neutral family, so the interface reads as a single material rather than a collection of panels. Controls are tactile and friendly: softly rounded, warmly filled, with one confident amber action per region.

Motion behaves like a print coming off the bed. Things rise into place and settle on a cubic ease-out; nothing bounces, glows or loops. Motion explains feedback and change, and it has exactly one authored moment: a freshly made thumbnail printing itself in, layer by layer.

The identity rejects three things. It is not a cold-grey IDE with a Microsoft-blue accent, not a corporate dashboard of identical metric cards and accent gradients, and not a neon gamer skin whose personality competes with the models.
keyCharacteristics: One warm neutral family (hue ~30–40°) from near-black bench to off-white filament. No cool greys in the canonical themes.
A single amber accent, reserved for action and selection.
Tonal layering for chrome. A soft shadow appears only under the user's models.
Fixed-size model cards in a wrapping gallery, at three user-chosen sizes.
Inter throughout, in a compact 10–18 px working range. Larger sizes are reserved for the About dialog.
Dark is the default theme. Light is its full counterpart.
Feedback-sized motion (120–180ms) with one authored moment, the print-in reveal; all spatial movement yields to the OS reduce-motion setting.

rules.name: The Amber Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the next action or the current selection, nothing else. One filled amber button per region (toolbar, details panel, dialog footer). Never use amber for panel fills, decorative strokes, headings or icons at rest.

rules.name: The Models Wear the Color Rule
rules.body: The user's thumbnails are the most saturated things on screen. If a new element out-shouts a thumbnail, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral in the canonical themes carries the brown-amber undertone. A pure or cool grey (#808080, slate, zinc) in the warm themes is a bug.

rules.name: The Every-Key-Every-Theme Rule
rules.body: A new color resource is added to all six theme dictionaries in `App.axaml` at once. No hardcoded hex in views (the confirmation dialog's `#FFC107` warning glyph and the attachment remove button's `White` are existing debt).

rules.name: The Weight Before Size Rule
rules.body: Step hierarchy with weight (400 → 600 → 700) and color (Ink → Graphite → Dust) before raising the size. Nothing in the main window exceeds 18px.

rules.name: The Uppercase Is a Shelf Label Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase is reserved for sidebar section headers. Don't uppercase buttons, field labels or titles.

rules.name: The One Left Edge Rule
rules.body: Everything in the sidebar starts 14px in: section headers, rows, the "Nova Categoria" affordance. New sidebar content aligns to it.

rules.name: The Lifted Model Rule
rules.body: Only containers that hold a user's model or its preview may cast a shadow. Toolbars, sidebars, panels, buttons and chips stay flat. Popovers and dialogs use the platform/Fluent default.

rules.name: The Corner Tag Rule
rules.body: Metadata laid over an image (file type, filename) is docked to an edge with only its inner corner rounded. It never floats as a free pill over the model.

rules.name: The One Icon Set Rule
rules.body: New UI uses the vector geometry in `App.axaml`, never emoji. A new icon joins the same family: solid fill, 16×16 bounds, similar ink weight.

rules.name: The One Moment Rule
rules.body: The print-in reveal is the only animation longer than 200ms. New motion is feedback-sized, or it replaces the reveal as the authored moment rather than joining it.

rules.name: The Gate Rule
rules.body: Any new transform, translate or scale animation goes under `:is(Window):not(.reduce-motion)`. Opacity and color may stay ungated.

dos: **Do** reference colors only through `{DynamicResource ...}` keys, and add any new key to all six theme dictionaries in the same change.
**Do** keep amber to one filled action per region, plus the selection ring and progress indicator (The Amber Is Earned Rule).
**Do** separate chrome with tonal steps and 1px `separator` seams. Reserve shadows for model cards and previews (`0 2 12 0 #28000000`).
**Do** use 32px-tall toolbar controls with 6px radius, and 14px horizontal padding for every sidebar row.
**Do** step text hierarchy with Inter weight and the Ink / Graphite / Dust colors before raising size. Stay at or under 18px in the main window.
**Do** dock overlay metadata to a thumbnail edge with a single rounded inner corner.
**Do** use vector `StreamGeometry` icons for anything new.
**Do** check new text against WCAG AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 for ≥18px or icons) on the surface it actually sits on, in Dark and Light.
donts: **Don't** introduce cool or neutral greys, a blue accent, or gradients in the warm themes. That is the IDE look PRODUCT.md rejects.
**Don't** build dashboard furniture: no big-number metric tiles, no identical icon-heading-text card grids.
**Don't** add neon, glow shadows or saturated chrome that competes with the models.
**Don't** put shadows on toolbars, sidebars, panels, chips or buttons.
**Don't** use `text-muted` for information the user needs to read; it is for disabled labels and resting borders only.
**Don't** hardcode hex values or `White` in views.
**Don't** take design cues from the Nord / Dracula / Solarized skins; they follow the warm system's roles, not the other way round.
